To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the Einstein's strength is a very useful concept for evaluating the stability of difference schemes for the chemical reaction-diffuction equations.

the strength of difference schemes of chemical reaction-diffusions equations is not a simple function of the strength of their differential counterparts and that it is not a monotonic function of the strength for the same differential equations.

1) the strength of difference schemes can be evaluated algebraically, 2) the Einstein's strength is a powerful criterion of the difference scheme quality, 3) the strength of schemes for chemical reaction diffusion equations is not a monotonic function of the number of the difference equations in a system.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the analysis of the strength of difference schemes of chemical reaction-diffusions equations.
the analysis of the strength of difference schemes, and in particular with the development of a difference algebraic approach to this analysis.
a comparative analysis of finite-difference schemes from the point of the Einstein's strong.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the difference algebraic approach provides a powerful tool to compare difference schemes of chemical reaction-diffusions equations and to estimate their strengths, and that it is possible to construct difference schemes for chemical equations which are more stable than the classical schemes.
, for the considered class of problems, the most effective and robust schemes are the schemes of second order in space and time.

the Einstein's strength is a powerful tool to evaluate difference schemes for reaction-diffusion and mass balance PDE systems, and that it is a useful criterion to select difference schemes for the simulation of reaction-diffusion processes.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the Einstein's strength is an important criterion for the analysis of the difference schemes and the numerical solution of PDEs.
the difference scheme of the second order in space and time for the Murray equation is the strongest scheme among the schemes analyzed.
the strength is a useful tool in the analysis of difference schemes.

, in the case of a system of PDEs, the Einstein's strength is a more powerful concept than the usual one for the analysis of numerical schemes.
the Einstein's strength provides a powerful and convenient tool for a qualitative analysis of difference schemes, which can be used for the construction of difference schemes for PDEs.
